title: resendMagicLink missing callbackURL — customer lands on server root
note: signInMagicLink called without callbackURL; magic link redirects customer to server root (port 3020) instead of frontend /dashboard. Same bug class as the fix applied to sendClaimLink — not propagated to this sibling procedure.

title: addEmailAndDispatchMagicLink missing callbackURL — customer lands on server root
note: signInMagicLink called without callbackURL in the GHL-placeholder-email staff flow. Same root cause as AC-05 — sendClaimLink fix was not propagated here either.

title: email param accepted in createUnclaimed but silently ignored — dead parameter
note: z.string().email().optional() declared in input schema; handler never reads input.email. Placeholder email is always generated regardless. Callers are silently misled. Remove the param or honour it.

title: softDelete has no guard for unclaimed profiles — leaves orphaned CP user row
note: Staff with customer_management:delete can soft-delete a profile while isUnclaimed=true. The corresponding control-panel user row (placeholder email) is not cleaned up. No claim path remains after deletion. softDelete should reject or warn when profile.isUnclaimed=true.
persistence: Writes is_deleted=true + deleted_at + deleted_source to customer_profiles; CP user row with placeholder email is NOT cleaned up.

title: createUnclaimed uses z.string().datetime() for dateOfBirth — rejects plain date strings
note: Zod 4 z.string().datetime() requires full ISO 8601 datetime (time component mandatory). Plain date strings like '2000-01-15' are rejected before the handler runs. The sibling upsertForCustomer at packages/api/src/routers/customer-profiles.ts:131 intentionally uses z.string().nullable().optional() without .datetime(). Inconsistency likely causes UI breakage for date-of-birth pickers.

title: createUnclaimed CP user insert has no conflict handling — ugly 500 on UUID collision
note: Placeholder email insert into control-panel user table has no onConflictDoNothing/onConflictDoUpdate. UUID v4 collision probability is ~0 but unhandled DB unique violation would surface as HTTP 500 with opaque error. Low real-world risk; cosmetic hardening only.
persistence: Writes CP user row on success.
